review:
EDIT FOR PATCH: The patch addressed a large number of gameplay, graphical, and audio glithces and included a number of Quality-of-Life improvements which, while welcome, were minor with regards to changing this reviewer's opinion. The biggest addition to the game is the new "Challenge Mode" which provides additional incentive to become better (read: faster) at playing the game. While this will appeal to many players (I haven't yet tried it, myself, but I intend to), this doesn't alleviate some of the glaring flaws of my review, the lengthy original of which I'll leave intact below this.

The one gripe I had that was listed as addressed was the intensity at which every single carnivore murders whatever they can, and despite the patch notes stating things have been fixed, from a couple hours of testing they have been mildly improved but certainly not fixed. Carnivores now wait much longer to murder herbivores, which is great for an open ecosystem - with the exception of the Dilophosaurus, which gleefully butchers anything it can whenever it can (3 Dilophosauruses kill 6 hadrosaurs in less than 3 minutes). Carnivores are also only supposed to hunt now as dictated by their need for food, which by my testing isn't quite accurate; it seemed to work on some carnivores, and was entirely unaffected by hunger on others.

None of the rest of my review issues have been improved upon so... my recommendation stays the same: buy on sale, or don't buy. 

Original review: I paid full price on release for this game and was extremely excited for everything that was advertized. Make no mistake, this is one of the most visually stunning JP titles ever. However, that's mostly where the good impression ends.

I managed to "beat" the game in two weeks. In that time there was a good deal of frustration and annoyance, and in the end the unlimited open sandbox of Isla Nublar is neither unlimited nor open so I haven't bothered to play it much after the first day of completing the game.

The dinosaurs are advertised as "intelligent." They are anything but. Their requirements are finicky and they can't determine what side of their own compound they should stay on to remain happy. The pack hunters never hunt in packs. ALL the predators are murderous psychopaths that will kill any other dinosaur they can the moment they have access to it rather than for food, and the herbivores have absolutely zero herd mentality for protection. The game is glitched as well in which thirsty/starving dinosaurs cold be standing by a mound of food/lake of water and not consume it, preferring instead to simply die. The slightest disruption will send them into a concrete-wall-breaking frenzy (even the small ones that shouldn't even be able to crack the stuff) after which they all once again go murder-happy.

The "quest" system is equally nonsensical. Three factions that are SUPPOSED to be working together have the twitchiest, most ludicrous egotism in that when one succeeds at ANYTHING, the other two get... jealous? Really? And if you haven't paid enough attention to the poor divas they will actively sabotage the park causing the DEATHS of possibly hundreds of people at a time. Over a temper tantrum. Because you didn't take a photo for them of a dinosaur drinking, or you didn't release a dinosaur with a specific, low-level advantage. It breaks immersion immensely, considering those scientists, marketers, and security people should be outright shot, never mind arrested, for being responsible for that idiocy. None of the above system is actually enjoyable or realistic, and it's somehow heralded as this game's version of park management.

In response to those temper tantrums or weather effects, you need to keep your park safe. Instead of doing that intelligently, you need to instead prep yourself for more stupidity than any park owner should have to. Power's gone out? Well, your teams are suddenly on strike or something because YOU, YOURSELF need to hop into a jeep to turn all the power back on manually. While driving the jeep yourself is a fun addition, being forced to do it for basic continuance of the park (usually during a multiple-issue crisis) is a waste of time and again an unrealistic distraction from the gameplay. With regards to the weather, none of the dinosaurs seem at all comfortable in rain. Some will even bust out of the compound in a panic (maybe they're related to the wicked witch of the East or something), but once they've escaped the rain is forgotten because now there's human squeak-toys to munch on.

Finally there's the unlocking/advancement system. While I understand what the developers were trying to do, it's another unnecessary time sink that you stop what you're doing every THREE MINUTES to send out a dig team across the world for the barest of samples for study. Why are dig teams returning with only what fits in their pockets? Why are my dig teams not instead staying at dig sites, getting the fossils and then sending them back by mail continuously until they're done with the site? How much fuel and time is wasted going back and forth, and how much time is wasted by me leaving the main window to go to the world one and send them back out for the fifteenth time to the digsite they're so familiar with they should be paying rent to it? And if it's a money concern, how is it that I am the same person running the same company of the same park that has entirely different accounts for money on each of all these small islands?

The silly thing is a lot of these failings could be overlooked if the end result was really impressive, and it's not. The buildable area of Isla Nublar (the sandbox you can access partway through) is unfortunately VERY small considering all the dinosaurs you might want to populate it with and the visuals, while stunning, are still just more jungle. The island boasts no money necessary, but still has hatchery failure so the one major drawback to having a dinosaur fail in the real game isn't in place but instead creates a new one where you might want to create a dinosaur tough enough to stave off predators instead goes insane becuase it needs three in a herd to be happy but you've only successfully hatched one of fifteen attempts. Which brings me to another issue: there's no possible way to create an open ecosystem. The predators are entirely psychopathic, and the herbivores are idiots. The carnivores will attack anyting they can because they exist, and will even impale themselves upon a Triceratops's horns because they have nothing better to attack. The herding animals will wander AWAY from each other, then get upset because tere aren't enough of them nearby even though they're the ones that wandered off. Conversely, an anti-social dinosaur (even the herding ones) will know instinctively how many dinosaurs are in even an extremely large enclosure and get upset about overpopulation, even as they get upset that they are alone in the one corner of the pen while the other three are in the other corner.

To sum up: this game has so much POTENTIAL but failed to deliver upon launch. It currently does not have the staying power and draw that other sandbox games do, while having some of the best features of a sandbox game (dinosaurs, naturally, but also the ability to drive a jeep, fly a helicopter, and use a Gyrosphere in the park alongside the guests). There are some really well-done moments (a pack of four or five Dilophosauruses being "social" by chatting and chirping among themselves and flicking their wrists is the most adorable thing in the game), which are overshadowed by things that are more frustrations and roadblocks than actual gameplay and content.

I might recommend this game when it goes on sale, considering there are now mods to help out with some of the failings. However, as someone who is not usually a "mod" guy, I have to give this one a pass at full price. A game at this cost and with this IP has a relatively high bar to hit, and clearly failed.

See this is a tough one. I'm really torn because the time I have spent in the game I have absolutely loved. The dinosaurs look amazing and being able to give them different colour palettes helps a lot in making the dinosaurs unique. However, that's pretty much where it ends. The dinosaurs don't really interact with each other in meaningful ways (like herding and pack hunting in JPOG), the buildings and attractions look bland and uninspired, the guests feel so soulless and boring, and the park altogether feels really dead. I think the issue here is the price. It is a perfectly good game, for maybe half the price it is now. At the current price it's just not worth it. I'm going to spend a lot of time in this game and I love it, but I think that's only because I really love the Jurassic Park franchise and dinosaurs as well. Looking at it without rose tinted glasses, well, it falls a bit short.

However, I do want to say this. I don't often post reviews, barely any actually, unless I think I have something important to say. I certainly do in this case. This game desperately needs the developers to continue to support this game and improving it like they do with their other games. I understand that they needed the game out now to match up with the Fallen Kingdom release. Another year of development and all these problems would probably be ironed out. I'm going to stick with this game and look forward to every improvement that Frontier brings. But, for everyone else, you're probably better off waiting for a sale or until the game gets some much needed depth.

Some much needed improvements:
Better AI (top priority)
Better guests (why not give different guests different needs? Carno lovers, families who love herbivores, etc.)
More structures (varied amenities, rides)
More animations for the dinosaurs (more kill animations, social animations)

Just more depth really. Right now it's like the best pool ever but it's so shallow I can only walk through it. It's so close to being something great that it pains me to not recommend it. But I optimistically wait for the future in hopes that Frontier will turn this into the best dinosaur game ever, and the sequel that Operation Genesis deserves. I will update to positive when I feel like the game has enough content and depth to warrant the full price.

I REALLY wanted to love this game but, unfortunately, it was a bit of a let-down. The graphics are beautiful and I do enjoy how they make it feel like a real Jurassic theme park but there are a several major issues that kept me from loving it. 

First of all, there is very little content other than the dinosaurs themselves;  you cannot customize the exhibits at all other than basic placement of water and plants, there are very few restaurants and other shops and there is absolutely no decorations or other park customization props. This makes the parks look very boring and uncreative.

Secondly, the power management was tedious to say the least. It was interesting, and even initially fun, that the power could go out and you would have to fix it before all hell broke loose but it became very tiresome after awhile (even with upgrades it was a constant headache). The power plants also take up way too much room and were hard to place becuase of terrain constraints. I felt like my park was always a third power stations or more which was extremely frustrating, especially when you have extremely limited room to begin with. 

Another thing that I was dissapointed about, was that there was no way to play "ethically." I was originally planning on playing as ethically as possible for my first playthrough and then going back and doing a fun and rather evil playthough of letting the dinosaurs eat the guests and whatnot. I was disappointed, however, to find that you are locked in to these unethical behaviors from the start. I tried to play ethically but almost instantly you're forced to let dinosaurs out to attack guests, and then you let some dinos starve in inhumane conditions for awhile, and then you make them fight to the death, and then, and then... it just keeps getting worse and there is nothing you can do about it except stop playing or do what they ask. I was very sad that there was no way you could steer the park towards being a safer and more ethical park.

Another problem was the lack of information for each dinosaur. I was constantly hatching dinosaurs and then realizing that they were not compatible with the exhibit I put them in. Once you hatch one of a species there should be some way of accessing all of it's information but there isn't and this is a major flaw in my opinion. Along the same lines, there is no way to access the information of an enclosure. If a dino needs say 50 tiles of forest, then there needs to be a way of seeing how many tiles of forest are in an exhibit but there isn't. 

My final major problem with the game was that it was way too easy for dinosaurs to break out of their enclosures. I shouldn't have to worry about a tiny dilophosaur breaking out of an electified concrete and steel fence! Having dinosaurs break out of the weaker fences makes sense but the smaller dinos should not be able to break the stronger fence types. If you're willing to pay a huge sum for a super stong fence, nothing but maybe an indominus should be able to break out of it. This is especially a problem since dinosaurs' happiness tends to be a little glitchy; they'll be perfectly happy on one side of the exhibit and then they move to the other side and are instantly unhappy and decide to break out.

I really want to say that I would recommend the game because I did have some fun during the several hours that I played it (though it was quite frusterating and stressful at times) but it just has too many major problems and there really isn't enough content to justify the price. I really wanted to love the game but, unfortunately, it had a tendency to be more frusterating than fun.

I'd like to start off with that I don't want to give the game a negative review, I really dont. It's a good game, but not $55 good. (or $60 in my case since I pre-order the dlx edition) I've been hooked on it since the moment it's released and playing every moment I can (it's not actually the full 35 hours i've played since release I just have a habit of leaving games open when im AFK). But the game has issues you just cant ignore. 

The dinosaurs are gorgeous but not much beyond that. They're well animated but have an extremely limited selection of animations. Dinosaurs lack a proper AI. They mindlessly roam around, and thats it. There is no hearding or pack-hunting. Carnivores just simply go on killing sprees, and dont stop when they're full, leaving a trail of death that would make the Indominus jealous, they literally will not stop killing things until they are dead or have nothing left to kill, making it impossible to make a balanced ecosystem. Dinosaurs require a minimum amount of grassland and forest depending on the dinosaur, this sounds good in concept but utterly terrible in design, you think you have what it takes to keep the dinos happy, but they move to the left 3 feet and the grassland/forest rating is totally different, leading for them to become unhappy and break out (which is why my trex broke out)

While the game is beautiful it lacks content and things to do. Visitors are just generated on pathways, no needs, not clickable, just math generated. Another thing that bothers me is the lack of cosmetics, the only thing you can really make your park better with is with the tree and grass tools which dont even allow you place trees seperately, its just a brush, leaving gaps in spaces where you could fit them on your own. I want benches, flower-beds, trashcans, picnic tables, parks, signs, etc but none of it is there. The game honestly doesnt have much to do, what you do in the first 20 minutes of your first game is the pretty much the only thing you'll be doing. Half the game is really just telling rangers to fill up feeders, because you can't do much else. There are no upgraded buildings or building variations, leaving your park looking bland. No different style or larger hotels, paddocks, shops, or anything, it feels unimpressive when you have tiny buildings dotted everywhere. The park honestly feels dead. 

The game's maps are small, which causes an issue because most dinosaurs require large enclosures meaning you can only fit a very limited selection of dinos on an island, or they'll break out. Isla Nublar, what was told be a large spacious sandbox map is very small as well, only being able to fit a few decent sized enclosures. The sandbox mode in Isla Nublar was terribly thought out. I'm a sandbox player, I don't enjoy playing through all these island campaigns to slowly unlock stuff, and that's an issue. You can only use what you've unlocked on Isla Nublar, meaning if you really want the open-endedness that the game can give you, you have to play through all the island campaigns and complete all the objectives. It's been over a day of obsessive playing and I still have yet to unlock everything when I just wanted to play the open-ended sandbox it should have provided. I'm already starting to get bored of the game, still chugging through on Isla Sorna and I haven't even been able to experience and enjoy a true sandbox experience. I honestly feel burnt out, and by the time I unlock everything I won't even have the interest to keep playing and enjoying like I should have. 

The game honestly feels like a stripped down Planet Coaster (don't even get me started), and Planet Coaster was already bad enough for me. Like PC and most other Frontier games, they're absolutely gorgeous, but extremely shallow in gameplay and what other content they offer, blow-up kiddy pool shallow. And it's a shame because I love the dinosaurs, I love how beautiful the game is. But it's not wortha $55/60 price tag. The games biggest saving grace would've been a modding community, but Frontier has this big thing against modding that I don't quite understand so the game comes with 0 modding support so you're stuck with what you got.

This game has so much promise and potential, but it feels absolutely wasted. I remain optimistic that Frontier will hopefully address these complaints and more and look forward to what they may have in store.

In its current state, it pains me to have to advise against a purchase. I myself loved Jurassic Park: Operation Genesis (JP:OG) and when Jurassic World: Evolution (JW:E) came out I really, really, REALLY wanted to like this game too, but unfortunately JW:E is surpassed or matched by JP:OG in every regard, with the exception of graphics and dinosaur diversity.

This is a bare-boned shell of a Park Simulator game. There are no guest needs or personality. You wouldn't even know there were guests if it weren't for sudden cashflow, as soon as dinosaurs make an apperance in your park. I grant you, there are the guest sprites, but thats all there is (I once had apparently more than 12.000 guests in my park and it didn't feel any different from having no guests in my park).

To sum up what major issues annoy me (excluding the everyday pet peeves):

- EXTREMELY shallow simulation of guests (they barely qualify as entities for this game)
- You are restricted to 5 small, claustrophobic islands for your normal gameplay and 1 claustrophobic island for a sandbox mode (they aren't even true islands, just cordoned off areas in an island skybox)
- There is no day/night cycle
- Only 3 real attractions (2 different viewing platforms and the gyrospheres (the equivalent of a fast-food restaurant doesn't constitute an attraction for me))
- No in-depth dinosaur AI (a simplistic general beavioural model with no herd/pack behaviour)
- Limited (and hence repetitive animations)
- Weirdly timed, often unfitting and repetitive (annoying) voice overalys
- A cluttered UI, making tasks like resupplying the feeders, treating a dino, etc extremely tedious
- Fences becoming useless as soon as a dino is uncomfortable (a 150kg raptor can apprently break (not scale) an electrified heavy steel fence without taking damage or being deterred)
- No customization for park buildings, no decorations, etc
- You can't kill your dinos (you can tranq and then sell them, but that is a tedious, time-consuming and a sometimes bugged process)
- Genetic modification has no apparent impact on dino behaviour or abilities (except increasing some numbers)
- Contracts are sometimes nonesensical with how the other factions disapprove of them (Science division wanted to not have any Carnivores eating guests for 10 min, but apparently that is something that the Security and Entertainment division disagreed with, as 10 min without any carnivores feasting on my guests put me in disfavor with the those factions)
- Sometimes you are also offered contracts which you cannot fulfil on your current island (and contracts don't carry to other islands)
- A shallow research system. Aside from unlocking new fences, variations on the fast-food store (gift shop, etc) and 2 of the 3 visitor attraction, it is pretty much just filler, just useless upgrades to improve some stuff here and there


The few truely good things about this game are the cosmetic customization of dinos, dino diversity, the graphics and dino rendering and that is just not enough to make a game. Especially considering this game was developed by the same studio, that developed Planet Coaster, this game is at its current version an embarassing failure and will only be enjoyable after considerable changes. This just feels like a rushed product to make the E3 deadline.

If you’re also one of those dinosaur enthusiasts who already spent a lot of time with Blue Tongue’s 2003 [i] Jurassic Park: Operation Genesis [/i] and always hoped for a worthy successor, then [i] Jurassic World Evolution [/i] is definitely a game you need to get on!

The cloning and care aspect in this game is amazing, and the many dinosaurs you can create from DNA samples and release into the park are gorgeous. Extending from the Early Jurassic Dilophosaurus to the terminal Cretaceous T-rex, the roster could indeed be a bit more diverse, especially in terms of the vastly underrepresented Gondwanan taxa, or the completely lacking Triassic dinosaurs. Nevertheless, the more than 40 different species you can choose from are still an enjoyable mix and they all have their own specific behavioral-ecological system you need to give attention to in order to ensure their health and happiness. Aside from their basic food and water needs, the dinosaurs can vary greatly in terms of their preferred habitat, enclosure size and the other species they can coexist with peacefully. This part of the gameplay is great. However, the depth of a number of other park building aspects still leaves a great deal to be desired: small decoration objects such as information and catering stands, restrooms or rocks would be very nice, not to mention more elaborate terraforming options or a couple more structures like the popular hot air balloon platforms to theme out and customize the park even further. Also, the Mosasaur water arena or the Pterosaur aviary and also a number of iconic dinosaur species such as the African Ouranosaurus and Carcharodontosaurus are sadly missing, and those would be a blast if they include them in a future DLC!

All in all, there is certainly a bell curve regarding fun and motivation with [i] JW Evolution [/i]. Starting as an exciting park management enterprise, it will eventually bring you to a point where you have researched every technology available, completed all genomes and built everything you can, and then it’s basically just about micromanagement and watching tons of money pour in. Therefore, it remains to be hoped the guys at Frontier take the potential for improvements and crank out even more expansion packs with new features. Regardless of the shortcomings and little weaknesses, I still think [i] JW Evolution [/i] is one of the most amazing games of 2018 and it definitely has a lot of untapped potential for awesome expansions in the future.

[b] Please read this review and if you enjoy/agree give it a thumbs up because i REALLY want Frontier, the development team to see this or for people to possibly pass it on.[/b]
 This review will be rather detailed and in-depth and having unlocked all the island and put a good near 50 hours into the game as well as being a fan of the original Operation Genesis Park Building game there is alot to go through.

Before i get into the review do i recommend it? Yes i do, if you're a fan of Dinosaurs, Jurassic Park and the PS2 park game you will likely have an enjoyable  experience here too. If you're sitting on the fence or none of the former points made however, i honestly believe you should wait and save your money and see what changes take place in the coming months then go from there. Alot needs adjusting, trust me.

[h1]Positives[/h1]

+ [b]Dinosaur variation[/b]
 I have no complaints here and while there are many famous dinosaurs that are heavily requested such as the Quetzalcoatlus and the Dimetrodon i have hopes they will appear later in the game (though their appearance and mechanics will obviously have to be unique). As far as i'm aware the Developers have already confirmed marine life and flying reptiles in future content. There are over 40 dinosaurs with more coming next week and i won't even be able to have all these dinosaurs in the 5 islands i've completed, there's that many!

+ [b]Dinosaur Design[/b]
By this i mean the depth to dinosaur gene splicing. Variation in colour and stat designs is a nice, engaging and refreshing way to make dinosaurs stand out and add some layer of depth to personalising. For the most part dinosaurs also look great, with the expection being the Giganotasaurus and Spinosaurus being way too small in comparison to the T-Rex

+ [b]Music/Sound Design[/b]
The game takes music from the films and adds some of its own. All in all i have no complaints here in the slightest. The dinosaur sound effects and animations while walking and running is spot on. My only complaint here is that the Spinosaurus is missing its signature roar from the 3rd film, though perhaps they've simply made it more subtle. 

+ [b]Factions/Quests[/b]
While the factions are interesting and fun to play around with especially when you get sabotaged, i also enjoy the continious contracts and the progression itself. It might seem grindy to people new to the genre but i think they've done a good job here. Nothing stays gated for too long and alot of the more popular dinosaurs are open quite early. The faction quests themselves also introduce some new gameplay mechanics or encourage you to test things out.

+ [b]Services[/b]
The inclusion of the jeep and rework on the Helicopters in contrast to the original game is great. I love getting hands on and driving around the park even if i can't run over customers (this kills the immersion when you're trying to rush through the park avoiding customers to repair something ASAP during a storm). The upgrades that you can put on park facilities is also a nice inclusion.

+ [b]Research and Dig Panels[/b]
I like how much more deep the research panel is and what it has to offer! Great work here! There are alot more dig panels and it works pretty much the same as Genesis with abit more variation which i appreciate.

+ [b]Difficulty/World Design[/b]
The difficulty of the game could have an extra 'hardcore' option but for a first playthrough i'm finding it fun and entertaining, but once you learn mechanics and have played through the first 2-3 islands it becomes progressively easier.

The world design is appreciated. Now don't get me wrong, i really want to have an island that is completely open to me for me to piss around in, and while i feel the campaign islands SHOULD be restricted in size to force you to adapt and change your playstyle to keep things refreshing, i do also think the Sandbox Unlimited Resource zone is still just too small. I'd like the restrictions to end at the ocean, not confined within an area of the island. 

[h1]Negatives[/h1]

- [b]Customers and Visitors[/b]
If you've played Operation Genesis i'm sure you'll know where i'm coming from when i say how annoyed i felt when i realised there was literally no customer interaction at all. Having customers have unique personalities based upon their group (thrillseekers, passivists, dino nerds) added a nice layer to that game, and is something that is surely missing here. You also can't click on customers, know where they're from, what they think of the park or anything (Outside of the menu telling you). Another issues i have regarding customers that was in OG (operation genesis) is that they don't showcase items they've bought, or pull out umbrellas when it rains. THESE CHANGES will not be that difficult to implement i'm confident, and it would VASTLY add to the games fun and replayability as well as immersion. Please fix this ASAP!

- [b]A.I (Customers and Dinosaurs)[/b]
In a nutshell, the dinosaurs need alot of fine tuning and adjustments if not new features implemented. Dinosaurs don't sleep yet they have animations for being tranqualised? Why not add their ability to sleep or watch them take a shit and things that they would definetly do? Again, this isn't a big thing but would add depth to the game. Furthermore there is no pack hunting, no "they do move in herds" regarding herbivours outside of brief, repeated communications that all species do the same. 1v1 fights are fun but can they not be tweaked to have 2v1 or pack hunting encounters? Why do Herbivores end up killing more civilians when they run loose than Carnivores? Why do Carnivores constantly want to kill everything even when they arne't hungry, meaning i can't put multiple herbivoures and carnivores into the same enclosure because they're all suddenly the Indominus Rex in personality? Why do Raptors headbutt and break out of heavy steel fences instead of climbing over it like in JPOG? Why can't i run customers over in my vehicle? Why can't dinosaurs attack and destroy my vehicle? Why do customers keep making the same continious pointing gesture continiously every 4seconds? Why don't customers and dinosaurs get caught up in the Tornado or sent flying and killed? I swear they literally did NOTHING with the customers and ignored some very simple slice of life changes when it came to dinosaurs.

- [b]Park Features[/b]
They basically need to add more. The monorail...i mean i know what it does now but i can't click on it or i can't see customers sat inside the monorail as they tour the park, instead it's a black window, felt really lazy tbh. I can't see customers sitting inside the bar, customers just walk through walls and doors when enterting buildings? The customers looking through the viewing domes have no animation and just stand there (about 20 at a time which is also lazy and shows a lack of care in how it is presented). Like this stuff isn't even that big to implement! Please just put some time and care into the details! I assume the balloon ride and safarai park from OG will be implemented as DLC which is fine, but at least let us see a stat base window of how our strucutres are fairing, how our customers feel and let us attribute certain park attractions to attune to certain customer appeal! In the livestreams Frontier boasted about micro managment yet it's not that important outside of stocking up food supplies and managing storms and bad weather.


[h1]Conclusion[/h1]

In conclusion the game is a solid 7/10 but with some fine tuning, added features and more sim building mechanics and some minor graphic tweaks and some good A.I. tweaks and easier of life and immersion features i could definetly stick it up to an 8/10.. 

P.S.  Also a proper SITE B would be appreciated because the Sandbox Island doesn't feel the same!

TL;DR: If you're a dinosaur fan, there's just enough here to keep you busy while you marvel at your prehistoric creatures.

[b][u]Full Review:[/u][/b]

[b]The good:[/b]
[list]
[*]The dinosaurs - This is the most important part of the game, and they have absolutely nailed it. They're lovingly rendered and animated and it never gets old to see a new one emerge from the Creation Lab, be it a mighty Giganotosaurus or a humble Archeaornithomimus. Some liberties have been taken with accuracy (this is [i]Jurassic Park[/i] after all) but not enough to be irritating. The models for the Edmontosaurus, Herrerasaurus and Suchomimus are especially nice in my opinion.
[*]Longevity - It took me 34 hours to five-star each of the main story islands and I haven't released all the dinosaurs yet. I picked this up on sale and feel like I got my money's worth.
[*]Jurassic Park - They've done a great job bringing the films to life. Personally, I'm more of a JP than a JW fan, but either way, it looks and feels just like a franchise of this scale should.
[*]Voice acting - Some good and some bad here. It's really neat to have Jeff Goldblum popping up every once in a while, and I also liked Dr. Dua's voice actor. But if I ever again hear Cabot Finch say "KNOCK KNOCK! WHO'S THERE? THAT'S RIGHT, NEW CAAAWNTRACT!" I'm going to dress up as a goat and jump into the nearest Velociraptor paddock.
[/list]

[b]The bad:[/b]
[list]
[*]The reputation system - God, this is dumb (and frustrating). There are three departments at your park - Security, Science, and Entertainment - who give you contracts and missions. Increasing your reputation with each of them, and completing their main mission on each island, is mandatory for technology and fossil upgrades. Here's the kicker - when you increase your reputation with one division, you decrease it with the other two. And when your reputation is low enough, they start sabotaging your park. Your Entertainment division should not be releasing your T-Rex to attack the guests because you didn't build an arcade! Which brings me on to...
[*]...The missions - You should be allowed to run your park the way you want to, and that means that you should not be forced to make dinosaurs kill each other to progress the story. The Security missions are especially bad for this - the second one has you staging a fight to the death between two small carnivores in order to unlock decent fences.
[*]Guest AI - It's non-existent. Guest management is extremely basic and essentially amounts to putting restaurants near viewing platforms.
[*]Micromanagement - The ranger team AI is dreadful - they take a really long time to do even the most basic tasks. So if you want something done, you have to do it yourself. That's fine when things are calm, but during a storm, when the power's out, the fences are broken and your dinos are rampaging? It's frustrating and not very fun. Also, the feeders have a really limited supply until you get to the final island. In the end, I was just demolishing and rebuilding feeders at huge expense rather than refilling them, just because it was so tedious. 
[*]Building - TERRAIN CONSTRAINTS BUILDING OBSTRUCTED TERRAIN CONSTRAINTS BUILDING OBSTRUCTED
[/list]

[b]The baffling:[/b]
[list]
[*]Comfort levels - Each dinosaur has a "comfort" rating which decreases if they are not housed appropriately. Eventually, if their comfort threshold is exceeded, they will break out and rampage. However, there are some crazy flaws with this system. For example, Stegosaurus require social groups of five or more to be happy. If they are in a large enclosure, and one of your five Stegos wanders off to the other end of it, the four remaining ones will forget it is there, break the fences down, and start killing guests! And there is no UI warning that this will happen until they are already rampaging!
[*]Enclosures - No dinosaur smaller than a T-Rex should be able to break a hole in a solid concrete fence.
[/list]

[b]Overall:[/b]
The park management aspect of this game leaves a lot to be desired. However, it wasn't offensively bad enough to stop me putting in enough time to five-star all islands on the main campaign. Really, it's a vehicle to keep you busy while you're unlocking and hatching new dinosaurs. I wouldn't recommend this to a general park management or strategy game fan, but I definitely would recommend for anyone like me who is playing for the dinosaurs. 
If you can get them on sale, I would also highly recommend the three dinosaur packs (Cretaceous, Carnivore and Herbivore) - the dinos involved add a lot to the game experience in my opinion.

I wish there was a "meh" option for reviews. This graphics for this game, the mechanics make a reasonable amount of sense, and a good amount of distinct dinosaur species to research and incorporate into your park. The behavior mechanics are limited, but what is there is interesting. Some people seem to have problems with bugs, but I haven't encountered anything yet and found the game runs pretty well overall.

But... it just gets a bit boring and repetitive. It plays a bit like a mobile game, with long stretches of time where you're just waiting for a dinosaur to incubate, or for enough money to tackle your next goal. There are no habitat requirements beyond finding the right mix of trees, water, and space. No dietary restrictions, or breeding. Guests are similarly shallow: There are no obvious bonuses to visitors for, say, building a particularly authentic habitat of species from one time period or contintent. There are supposedly different types of guests, but they all act the same. Once I got over the cool factor of having your my own dinosaur park, my enjoyment of the game dwindled.

So, I am not sure it's entirely fair to NOT recommend this game. It's fine, really. But it fails to live up to its potential. If you buy it, get it on sale.

As some people have said before, Jurassic World Evolution is not as good as a park simulator (Roller coaster tycoon 2, for example, is way better) as it should be. It would be amazing if it was a Roller coaster tycoon 2 with dinosaurs - what you would, in fact, expect from it -, but it fails in some controls, crowd control and mechanics in general. It IS impossible to not be mesmerized by the dinosaurs, though. Unlocking islands and new species make you want to keep playing to see the new stuff. It *still* feels kind of not as good as it should be, though. The dinosaurs have levels of comfort and different personalities depending on their species - which I think it's awesome - but it still feels like something is missing. 

When I was playing by myself, I really didn't feel like going much further, but after trying to play with friends I saw that you can easily get invested in creating more dinosaurs and completing missions. It is far from perfect (a 6.5~7/10 in my opinion), but still a lot of fun... And also a game where you can make a dinosaur themed park, which really is amazing by itself.

This is another very conflicted negative review, as many of them are for this game. There is a ton of potential, and even as it stands now, there are worse ways to zone out for a few hours than by hatching raptors and letting them loose on the unsuspecting public (although how unsuspecting can they really be? guest fatalities are treated like a normal everyday cost of doing business in this world and yet the people keep piling into the park).

The main problem is that there is absolutely no depth or challenge to this game at all.  The first way that this stood out to me was the complete lack of interaction with the guests in the park. They are essentially just window dressing. You can't click on them and see needs/preferences etc. They dont even arrive at the arrival point. They just sort of spawn in increasing numbers out of buildings and viewing  posts as you grow your park. Income isn't generated by specific guests buying tickets to the park, or items at the shops.  Its just a $$$ per minute thing that scales up as your park rating goes up and you build more attractions and shops.  Obviously the dinos should be front-and-center, but the complete lack of any kind of strategy/management aspect to this game is a massive letdown. 

Its also basically impossible to lose in this game. Sometimes it takes a while to build up momentum in the early game depending on your choices, but once you're going, there's no stopping you as you just print massive sums of money and basically have no incentinve to spend wisely or plan strategically. There is a "sandbox" mode that you unlock after a few hours of the campaign, but the campaign itself might as well be sandbox mode in terms of money. Again, a big disappointment for anyone who thought this was going to be a park management sim.

As for the dinos,  they look great but again, its shallow. They don't really have any kind of behaviours whatsoever. They can "panic" and run around a bit. If they get too uncomfortable, they can bash a hole in the fence. And they can eat. That's about it.  There is no kind of pack hunting or meaningful interaction between dinos. Certain dinos can "fight" each other, but again its just a one-on-one kind of duel (even if its actually a pack of 5 vs 1) and there are very few animations.  

There also isnt much to do for them in terms of habitats or maintenance. You balance out the amount of trees vs water vs grassland, and make sure there is a suitable amount of friends in the exhibit with them. That is the extent of it.  There are no play objects or design choices beyond the single type of trees/grass/water.  Once you've built one dino exhibit, you've essentially built them all.

It pains me to give a negative review because I don't see why they couldnt build a real game out of the foundation they have here, and I still hope that happens, either with updates/DLC or a sequel eventually. But right now, this game does not come anywhere close to justifying its price tag.

EDIT:  I just noticed there is already a $10 DLC for this game to get 5 more dinos....  I am no longer pained by leaving a negative review. Eff these people.  Already milking a shallow shell of a game with overpriced DLC.

The long review:

I cannot recommend this game in its current state. Here's why:


- The AI of the dinosaurs is very basic (no sleeping, no herding/packs, carnivores kill things just for the fun of it even when not hungry) and predictable. A 15 year old game (JPOG) had better AI.
- Canned killing and fighting animations. It is not exciting watching a small herbivore or person just stand there waiting to be killed. 
- Fighting animations seem to have been recycled for all species of the same 'type' (large carnivores will fight in the exact same stance, for example, with no variation according to species). This is incredibly lazy and I expected better from Frontier.
- Island map size is way too small for the sandbox island. Buildable area is even smaller and is sometimes arbitrary on islands.
- Lots of unneccessary busy work to the point of being tedious. Possibly put in place to hide the poor dinosaur AI, because after all...you are often too busy to even look at or enjoy your dinosaurs.
- Genome modification is neat, but it is just changing a bunch of stats. Doesn't really add anything to the gameplay and it does not hold my interest as much as it should.
- The pathing behaviour of the Jeeps is frustrating, sometimes they get stuck for no apparent reason and you have to take control manually.
- Placement of buildings/paths is buggy and frustrating, sometimes there are 'terrain constraints' or obstructions when there isn't anything remotely wrong.

Do you remember the feeling when you watched Jurassic Park for the first time? The excitement and the dinosaurs was amazing! This game comes quite close to it for me. Jurassic World Evolution is not the best or the most complex management sim on the planet and that's totally fine. The point of the game is the dinosaurs and they look gorgeous. This game made me feel happy and fuzzy inside and I loved to photograph my dinosaurs.

Pros:
- Great looking dinosaurs.
- Great graphics in general.
- Music is fantastic.
- Nostalgia is real.
- Characters have great lines.
- Jeff Goldblum. Enough said.

Cons:
- Not as challenging as it could be.
- Placing buildings can get frustrating.
- Management is minimal.
- No fast-forward option.
- No joint budget between islands.

In the end, most people will enjoy this game for the dinosaurs. It's a great dinosaur management game and visually beautiful. I used a lot of time in this game, and I can definitely say that it is worth it. I do think 44,99€ for the basic edition is a little too much though.

I want to like this game. I want really, really badly to like this game. It's absolutely stunning on a graphical level, and it blasts the brain with the childlike seratonin of "HOLY CRAP! But the more I played, the more I realized... this ain't no Dino Digs. I kept running into 'missing' features--are these buildings even making me money? Are the infamous dinosaurs of the Jurrasic Park franchise really this easy to please? Where the HELL is the pause button?! And eventually it hit me: They aren't missing. They weren't meant to be there, because this isn't meant to be a park manager.

Now, I could deal with that, I could readjust my expectations. Hell, I got the thing for five bucks in a 90% off sale, I figured there *might* be a reason. But you know what genre this game feels like? A mobile game. You know the kind I'm talking about. There's literal real-time timers in some parts of the game, reinforcing this. You know how infuriating it is to play those kinds of games without spending money? Yeah, you don't even have that option here. Just plop down buildings, solve every problem and unhappy dinosaur in 30 seconds, and wait, wait, wait.

Very glad I waited for such a deep sale. I can see $5 of appeal. Just... not much more than that.

I'd recommend buying this on sale, but would not recommend buying it at full price. 

Pros: its a dinosaur themed builder game that is pretty fun while you learn and unlock the gameplay mechanics. 

Most builder games are good right up until you learn and unlock enough to discover what the end-game is going to be, and this one falls apart at that point. 

Cons: Because the theme park management and design aspect of the game is shallow, game difficulty is artificially created. Virtually everything is locked behind multiple levels of menus, clicks, and cooldowns even where it should clearly be automated. Bad weather is leaned on too heavily, and certain maps are played entirely at night or dusk so it is hard to see. Space constraints in early maps create an interesting difficulty, but render most dinosaurs useless as the big popular ones win the game and take up space. 

By the time you get to the fourth island you're thinking that finally you'll get to build a park without the constraints listed above, but you quickly realize that the game is shallow without those constraints and the menu-game is still egregious. In the fourth island you have plenty of space to build shops, enclosures, and hotels safely, so the only difficulty left is the menu system. To finish this map you have to gather 100% of genome information for a selection of dinosaurs. This is entirely done in point-click-wait menus, and there is nothing to do while you wait because park management is negligible. This is the point where I put the game down. 

Ultimately, there are aspects of this game, such as first person mode and gene-editting that just should have been sacrificed for more in depth park management aspects. This would have saved them from having to hide difficulty behind chores and literally making it hard to see the game.

Jurassic World Evolution is a management game that makes all the franchise' fans happy like never before. 
The structure and the interface, are simpler in order to fit better to console platform, but could not be appreciated entirely by the more intransigent experts of the genre. 
Anyway, if you love the big lizards lived in the prehistoric age, this title is a must have.

Would I recommend this game? Yeah but only on sale. The dinosaurs are stunning, and let's be honest, that's what most of us are here for. But for me, I really wish they'd put in a PROPER sandbox mode.

The game in it's entirety is ok, but it's not infallible. 

Before I get into it, i'm not perfect either. I'll make edits as I remember things and if things are corrected. 

Here are my Pros and Cons.

Pros

-It looks good. Great textures, animations, and the grass even looks better than in some bigger scoped games.

-It sounds amazing. The dinos all sound good and with a proper illusion of distance when necessary. Even the starter motor sound for the 93' Jeep skin is correct, it sounds exactly like a 4.0L I6 Jeep engine.

-Setting up exhibits is really satisfying. It's not just throwing animals in a pen and making a path for people to see. Instead you have to figure out how certain dinos fit in with others OR you can genome edit the entire behavior of a dinosaur later in the game. I feel like that it gives it some necessary depth AND allows for increased creativity.

-Managing the needs of your guests is easier than making PB&J. Like nearly impossible to fuck up unless you're illiterate, dyslexic, or you're purposely torpedoing your own park. The various needs of the guests are centered around the exhibits and hotels and there are easily accessed "percentage of guests satisfied" data metrics. (My only original gripe was it seems pretty damned flagrant of FDev to not include restrooms at launch. It just makes no sense to me that FDev could be so involved in RCT franchise but it would take them over a year to think of toilets. Wtf? If you haven't played in a while you now have to start over OR rearrange your old parks to accommodate.) 

Cons

-The most obvious annoyance in the beginning are the time gates. It feels like a mobile game sometimes, why not have a mini game for the fossil extraction instead of just watching a timer tick down?. (Pro in the Con: I feel like this is partially made up for by the interactivity of the Ranger jeeps and ACU Helos. They give you something to do while waiting, and once you get a park going you will have plenty to work on with how spastic the dinos are)

-The dinosaur path finding logic, is what any person should consider "stupid".  I first chocked it up to just dinos being stupid, but after some further testing I now feel that it was made "good enough" and left as is. Dinos survived for hundreds of millions of years without human interaction, but now these guys are incapable of even finding new areas for food or water inside an enclosure? Inside bigger enclosures, they will not leave an area until they are uncomfortable enough to go attack a fence. If moving to attack a fence gets them closer to a less crowded area, they'll still attack the fence FIRST and then meander off instead of focusing on fixing their own fucking needs. Dinos already sprint to the nearest body of water after being released regardless of the distance they have to travel. If there's fence between the hatchery and pond it'll make dinos run around the ENTIRE map (map permitting) to get there and they'll ignore every other pond they happen to walk past on the way there) 

And that's not even the stupidest part. Upset dinos don't care if the fence they attack is actually a functional section. You can place a few open sections of fence in the center of your enclosure and if that's closer, they'll attack that fence instead of your real one. Seriously doubt that's intended gameplay. My suggestion would be to just "handwave" some explaination about how the dinos can smell food/water from miles away. Have the dinos "check" the population around feeders before moving there or something. That would make the same true for the smells of other dinos.

Being that I own 3 of their 5 current games (PC,JW, and ED) I think I'm in a good enough to position to NOT recommend this or any of FDevs "new" games. They all feel like they only gave themselves enough time to get about half their ideas in.

They also have a habit of not reiterating on features in all of their games. i.e. ED is my favorite VR game, but VR isn't even going to be part Odyssey at release.



(2025) with 2 out and 3 on the way, it really doesn't seem that FDev will do anything great for a while.

There's a lot to be said about the game in its current state. I bought the game a few days after release not knowing what to expect. I wasn't even aware it had been in development until I saw it advertised on Steam. I watched the trailer and glanced over the screenshots. A park simulator with dinosaurs? Well, for someone who loves both park sims and dinos I just had to give it a chance.

A little over 70 hours in, every island and reward unlocked, every mission and dinosaur genome completed, I think I've given the game a fair shot.

Visually it's a stunning game. I must've spent at least 5 minutes just starring at my first dinosaur when it had been released. It was only a little one, a Struthiomimus to be specific. I kept playing, kept making enclosures and releasing dinosaurs. The hours flew by and the magic was still there once I finally got to release my first T-Rex. By now I've incubated at least a dozen of them but I still watch the animation when I release them. The same goes for the raptors and Brachiosaurus. The game looks really good and there's just something really satisfying watching your dinosaurs roaming around in their enclosures.

Every now and then while working on one of your parks you might hear your T-Rex roaring or a Brachiosaurus... doing whatever it does in the distance and it just feels right. You'll be overlooking your park and might feel a real sense of accomplishment while watching your dinosaurs drinking water in the lakes, running through the trees and roaming over the hills. You'll probably wish that you could view the park through the eyes of the guests. Maybe be able to sit down and watch from the viewing galleries or viewing platforms. But you'll soon realize that it isn't possible. That feature isn't included in the game, and it's unfortunate.

The campaign is very linear and at times quite slow. Still, there's something there that motivated me to complete it and return to every island to unlock everything. Despite being extremely frustrating sometimes I still find that it was rather okay. Not expectional, but not bad either. I enjoyed it.

So after completing the campaign and unlocking everything I went on to the final island. It's the sandbox island and this is where you'll see that the game really does have some issues and may even be lacking in some aspects. First and foremost, for being a sandbox it's rather small and doesn't really allow you to build whatever kind of park you wish. You'll have to limit yourself to the confines of an already set area. Not exactly what I was hoping for but I was still able to have some fun with it.

You'll make pathways and place buildings and if you haven't already noticed during the campaign -the building mechanics are a bit confusing and extremely frustrating. A lot of times you won't be able to place a building where it seems it really should be able to be built because of "terrain restrictions". You'll find that it usually boils down to the ground not being flat enough, but I hope Frontier makes it easier for players to see what's actually the issue.

After a while you may also notice that there seems to be a lack of variety when it comes to buildings. It eventually gets a bit boring to have the same fast food, gift shop, restaurant and bowling alley buildings all over the parks. There's not even decorations. Not a single item. Considering Jurassic World Evolution is a park simulator this is seriously disappointing.

So you've made enclosures for your dinosaurs, you've placed feeders and put trees and water in there. Now you've got to figure out which dinosaurs can live together and what requirements they have. You'd think that at least the latter would be conveniently displayed on a tab or something for each dinosaur in the Creation Lab... but you'd be wrong. Instead at this point you'll either have to figure it out and keep notes yourself or do what I did and find a spreadsheet online that someone so kindly has put together for everyone else. It really should be in the game though.

You'll incubate some dinosaurs and inevitably you'll want to make some giant herbivores, like Diplodocus or Brachiosaurus, to put in your park too. Diplodocus is easy to keep comfortable but Brachiosaurus, Camarasaurus and Mamenchisaurus are quite challenging. There's got to be an almost perfect balance of trees, grassland and enclosure size for them to be comfortable. It's actually a bit too difficult in my opinion and really needs some rebalancing. Either that or, as previously stated, some convenient information tab would be much appreciated before releasing the dinosaurs.

Either way, you've got your buildings, your enclosures and your dinosaurs. Everything is looking great. It's just that you have to keep resupplying the feeders constantly and after not too long your dinosaurs are going to start dying off. At this point the game is going to start to feel more like a dinosaur management game rather than a park simulator. It's frustrating and tedious to resupply the feeders this often. There should either be upgrades to increase the capacity of the feeders or an option (at least on the sandbox island) to turn off the feeders need to be resupplied.

It's pretty much the same story with the dinosaurs ageing. Sure, it wouldn't make sense if the dinosaurs didn't die from old age but the problem is that it happens too fast. It needs rebalancing in my opinion because this too gets quite tedious. It feels like the dinosaurs should stay alive at least twice as long as they currently do. Otherwise what's the point of being able to name them if you have to replace them before long? Also, the option to turn off dying from old age would be nice in the sandbox mode.

Regardless, you may end up having a fully functional and beautiful park that is just a gem to look at. You'll be overlooking it and feel like you'd want to be one of those guests walking around down there and experience what they do. You'll be wondering what the guests are thinking about your park, but you won't really find out. You can see where they want shelther, food, drinks, fun and shopping but that's it. You won't know what your guests really think about your dinosaurs and it feels like that's what the game kind of should be about... Creating a beautiful dinosaur park and having guests enjoy all of it. As of now, the guests are just there. Wandering around not thinking anything about your main attractions.

So with all of that being said, would I recommend the game? I think so, yes. I've gotten over 70 hours out of it already and I still want more. The problem is that when I play Jurassic World Evolution now it feels like I have done everything I can do, and it's really up to Frontier to make me want to come back and play it again. And I hope they do, because this game has so much potential it would be a real shame otherwise.

After Playing a While

After playing it for a little longer there are a few things to add, but the biggest thing is that while the game as it is plays well, it does feel unfinished. I keep getting the feeling I'm playing an Early Access game rather than a fully polished one. Dinosaurs walk through the food releasee things instead of over or around it. 

You can't really interact with guests either, and this is really the most 'unfinished' feeling part of the whole thing. In Zoo Tycoon, for instance, you had to take care of putting down food and drink stations, setting up garbage cans and benches, and guests would compain if they couldn't see animals. In this game you place paths and viewing areas but they don't seem to really have any effects on the guests. Guests just sort of pour in no matter what you do. It's nice not struggling to make money all the time and speding hours waiting for it to build up, but at the same time it takes away a lot of customization and fun.

The dinosaurs themselves could use a little more individuality as well. The coats are exact clones unless you add genes, but then you get all clones of the new color. I like that you don't have to count how many trees are in the enclosure or how many squares of water you put down, but I would like to see a little bit more in terms of building an enclosure. As is it's just... fence, viewing spot, water puddle, couple tree taps. Rarely you get a picky species that wants a little more water or trees but for the most part they're all pretty much the same. 

I would like to see more streamlining of the interface. Right now if you want your Ranger crew to refill the trough, you have to pull the ranger menu up, pick a crew, select Add new task, and then click what you want them to do. Its the same to tranq an animal or fix a fence or treat a sick dino. There has to be a better way than going through all that! Maybe just having it pick an unoccupied crew first followed by the nearest crew available to carry out the task? It's not terrible as it is, but it's definitely a lot of unnecessary action that delays tranqing rampaging dinos and allows them to kill 15 people while you pick a crew. That ain't good for my star rating. :P Like, IDGAF which crew does the job as long as it gets done.

Finally the realism is lacking one more thing. When a dinosaur kills another dinosaur or a guest, there's no blood. I understand some people don't want to see it and that's fine to make it an option you can turn off/on. But when I have to wait for the interface to tell me there's a dead dinosaur because I can't tell from looking at it if it's dead or just injured, something is wrong. When two dinosaurs fight I have to hover over them to see their health points because I can't tell who is the most injured. That's... quite unrealistic and does break the immersion a bit. I don't need chunks of flesh flying through the air but some indication of injury besides a point count would be nice. 

All of that said I've still been having a blast. The game is still a lot of fun and I still recommend it. Whether or not these issues are game breaking really depends on what you enjoy most about the game. If you're the type that played Zoo Tycoon and liked to plan out perfect little paths with streetlamps and garbage cans and little sitting areas, you may not enjoy this as much. Which doesn't mean it won't be fun for you but you may prefer to wait for a sale. If you just want to play with dinosaurs in some casual fun, you'll like this one.

What could possibly go wrong when managing an island full of dinosaurs? A lot actually but none of it leads to amazing gameplay. With so few actually good scenarios to go through, and a lack of content plus a humongous amount of repetitiveness Jurassic World evolution has me all but coming up with what Jeff Goldblum said in Jurassic Park, "that is one big pile of shit." 

I think i can speak for most people who negatively reviewed this, we all wanted the game to be as spectacular as the trailers hyped us up for. A new Jurassic Park game with next gen graphics and the successor to Jurassic Park Operation Genesis? Oh boi i can’t wait! The first day it came out i was playing it immediately, so excited to see and play with no idea of what i was walking into. I guess the first moment of repetitiveness was when i got to Isla Pena. Up until this moment the game had my full attention and i was loving it. I noticed that i hadn’t unlocked any buildings or new dinosaurs. I then had to go back to the other islands and complete contracts to be able to unlock the things i wanted to be able to play correctly. Ohhh uh okay. This led me into a 6 hour battle with sabotage and other things when all i’m wanting to do is unlock some buildings and dinosaurs. Then i started to figure out that this was the entire game, and other issues started popping up that screamed lack of content or needs to polished a lot more. For the purposes of this review i will go in depth on each issue and explain what’s wrong and why. As Samuel L. Jackson once famously recommended, “hold onto your butts.”

At the beginning of the game you are taught the basics of construction and dinosaur creation then introduced to the first problem in game (right of the bat) the three divisions that make up your park's staff: science, entertainment, and security. Each of these divisions offer contracts that, when completed, give you cash and raise your reputation with that division to unlock items, dinosaurs, and buildings plus also furthering the division’s story mission. While contracts are a good source of money in the early game, they come with an odd complication: completing contracts for one division lowers your reputation with the other two. This creates a nonsensical balancing act that, whilst not difficult to overcome in the long run, feels arbitrary in context. If you do not balance the contracts between the three divisions however things start to get dicy. The divisions start to hate you for not giving them enough attention and then will sabotage the entire park to get you to give them attention. This ranges from turning off the power to legit opening the gates and allowing your flesh eating monster dinosaurs out to kill visitors without any remorse. In the real world they would be in prison. This is unrealistic and frankly annoying as shit to deal with. I get it’s to add stuff for you to do in the game but none of this is enjoyable. To unlock certain items you have to complete contracts with a certain division. To do this in a timely manner you have to not to do contracts with the other two divisions so you can unlock the thing you want but this almost always results in sabotage. Unless you like sitting for hours upon hours to do contracts with each division so you can keep them happy there is no way around this. Here’s the repetitiveness i was talking about. It already is beyond repetitive to do contracts now they have this shit. This also gives me a question, why do you need a research center when the only way to unlock new things is to use the contracts with the divisions? I’d be more than okay with having the ability to unlock things with the divisions if you could also unlock them with money in the research center. I guess it just adds to an already boring building variety that does nothing more than just be there. Which leads me into my next topic, visitor content. 

When creating a Jurassic Park management sim you have to have more than just really beautiful dinosaurs. Now while i give frontier credit for creating these absolutely beautiful dinosaurs they absolutely did jack for the visitor side of the game. Buildings are boring and really add nothing. No customization options or the ability to make the park feel like yours. Half of the buildings legit don’t even allow you to do anything with them. They are just there. Building in this game is also very dull and i don’t want to say that but it’s the god honest truth. The reason building is so dull is that most of the maps are tightly constrained, there’s no room for creativity and i’m all for creativity. Harkening back to my original point, even when there is room there is very little customization options to choose from and even then if the land you try to put your building on isn’t perfect then you won’t be able to put it there. The island’s are too small and the buildings are not customizable enough nor have the variety needed for this game. It’s as if all of frontier’s attention was on how beautiful the dinosaurs looked and not anything else. Visitor AI is also horrible. It’s beyond obvious they spent no time on this as every visitor is the same generic model and does the same generic stuff. I got really good to say about this visitor and building system in this game. It really sucks and frontier can do so much better. 

Dinosaurs break out too easily. This is really one of the worst parts of the game. You spend all this time doing contracts, unlocking new fences so you can actually get say your Tyrannosaurus and then five minutes later if the dino isn’t happy at all with his pen, he can break out of your max tier fence like it’s absolutely nothing. In the first Jurassic Park (movie) the fence was JUST electric and until the power was off, the Tyrannosaurus couldn’t and didn’t get out. Here you have ELECTRIFIED CONCRETE and not only can a Tyrannosaurus get out but raptors and other SMALL carnivores can get out too with no problem. What the fuck was going on in frontier’s mind when they did this. I mean seriously. It’s unrealistic and a bitch to know that even with all that work to get the right fence for the right dinosaur, it still can get out like nothing. Your dinosaur’s health doesn’t get lower from attacking the fences either. Holy jebus. Operation Genesis was made in 2003 and it didn’t have the problems this 2018 triple AAA game has. At least then dinosaurs health would go down by attacking the fence which is realistic. 

Dinosaur AI in this game is also a problem which begs the question, did frontier put remotely any thought or time into this other getting out what was absolutely needed for their paycheck. Dinosaurs don’t act like dinosaurs. When they fight, it looks generic as fuck and whenever dinosaurs fight they go into the same animation and do the same things. Not only that but if your enclosure isn’t absolutely perfect in every spot dinosaurs will flip shit and try to get out. But you got your higher tier fence, they couldn’t possibly….ohhhh…..then you got your Dinosaur feeders that need to be restocked, manually every 2 or three minutes. This has been a community wide ugh and frontier has noticed and is updating this to fix it so props to them for that. 

There’s more issues but due to the length of this review i feel the need to end it here. This game had the potential to be one hell of a game. Is it worth $60 dollars, absolutely no. When it comes on sale and is cheaper then maybe i’ll recommend it. Frontier has promised to update it and fix the problems so there is hope it will eventually be better but as for now, save your money and buy a better game. After careful consideration, I’ve decided not to endorse this park. 

Edit: Of my 168 hours, a large majority of this was having the game open on my desktop waiting for contracts to end so i could progress. And is my opinion of this game totally negative, no, and i do still enjoy playing it? Yeah to a certain degree. Just not enough to really recommend it.

Keeping it short:

I love the concept and the visuals, it does deliver a great impact.

However there is a lot of space to improve and I hope they will be working on it. The problems are in order of relevance:

1. [b]Maps too small [/b]: this is a tragic problem, it's okay to havecramped space on Isla Pena as that's the challenge, but all other islands are large, Nublar is potentially huge,  but in th end they are all almost the same size: small. You can never realize a "true" Jurassic Park, it will look more like a very small sector. 

- [b]Solution[/b]: please enlarge those maps, leave the whole island to be playable, they are not that big it shouldn't be hard.


2. [b]Fences are useless [/b]: What's the difference between a light steel fence and electrified Concrete one? Few seconds. A Gallimimus will break through the hardest fence with ease. That shouldn't be possible if not for the largest dino. 

- [b]Solution[/b]: Change how the fences react to damage, limit or nullify the damage that smaller dinos can do to heavy metal or concrete fences. Smaller predators with strong teeth like raptors could maybe damage heavy steel fences but it should take pretty long time, not just seconds. Also electrified fences should hurt the dino and make it panic when is low health. They will still take it down eventually, but it will take far more time / they will look for weaker spots.


4. [b]Difficulty[/b]: This is a really easy game, you can't lose. After the first few minutes you rack up millions, you can literally open all fences and let dinosaurs rampage through guest and you will still make profit. Penalties are too low, they are penalizing only in early game, but after that you can just sedate the dinos, wait few minutes and be on profit again, since all the structures and teams will stand intact. You don't even need to intervene during a sabotage, just recollect few escaped dinos and it will be fine. Crisis are a joke, a minor annoyance.

- [b]Solution[/b]: Escaping Dinosaurs should affect the park structures too after some time: they could attack rangers by forcing you to rebuy the squad, smaller predators could enter buildings and disable them by killing the personnel, larger dinos could damage pilons or some structures so you need money to restart or rebuild them, they could disable acu building personnel, etc. This way you will start care for guests and shelter, as now penalties from lawsuits could really disable your operation and forcing you to restart or to back to another island to gather resources.  Eventually debts should impact other islands as well although this is not critical as in the worst case you just restart the island. This could be a challenge in designing a good park and in managing storms, sabotage or any other crisis (if in combination with point 1 and 2).

Last:
[b]What would be making this game great if added [/b]: 

- More Buildings from the movies: Jurassic Park original visitor center, Water establishments, Avian domes, docks.
- More dinosaurs: Water dinos, Flyings dinos, Very small dinos that could roam freely and seldom becoming a danger (like the Compy, eating dong from dinos, would add to welfare)
- More Landscaping: Rivers, Lakes and waterfalls, Rock ridges, etc. They might even be very expensive but it would add a lot of complexity. You should be able to terraform mountains and hills to expand buildable area if you have crazy amounts of money to spend (Maybe keep only the arrival point Static, although it would be cool to be able to create more arrival points, even from the sea).
